items.title: Pupil dilation indicates arousal-related mediation of perceptual belief updating across auditory domains
items.author: Robert Baumgartner
items.content: In this study, pupil dilation is related to latent variables of belief updating (surprisal, information gain) from an auditory change-point task across the spatial and temporal domain. The results suggest arousal to modulate belief updating on an automatic perceptual level across the tested domains.

items.title: Successful coordination emerges from aligned self-predictions in a dynamic motor interaction
items.author: Fumihiro Kano
items.content: Combining eye-movement, body-kinematics, heart-rate, and individual-characteristic data with machine learning, this study shows that coordination during dynamic motor interaction reflects how similarly partners predict their own actions.

items.title: Improving the comparability of momentary affect assessments and accounting for item-specific effects in within-person affect dynamics
items.author: Jana Holtmann
items.content: The paper introduces a model for item- and person-specific affect dynamics that improves cross-study comparability when item sets only partly overlap, demonstrated in a reanalysis of five intensive longitudinal datasets.

items.title: People use roles to quickly predict how others will act, what they know, and when they can be replaced
items.author: Julian Jara-Ettinger
items.content: Using a self-paced reading paradigm, we show that, from just the mention of a role, people build rapid expectations about how other people will act, what they know, and whether they can be interchangeable with others in the same role.

items.title: Education about gender development predicts support for transgender youth’s gender identity autonomy
items.author: Analía F. Albuja
items.content: This study found adults believed transgender youth develop gender identity later relative to cisgender youth. This belief was linked to support for gender autonomy-limiting policies. An intervention regarding gender development reduced this belief, and increased support for gender autonomy.

items.title: High-level prediction of continuous speech during mind-wandering
items.author: Leon Y. Deouell
items.content: This study examines how spontaneous drifts in listening relate to EEG responses to continuous speech, using encoding models of semantic and contextual representations. It finds that neural markers of prediction, surprisal, and word meaning persist when the mind wanders away from speech contents, even as perceptual responses weaken.

items.title: A game-based intervention promotes social-cognitive development in early childhood in urban poverty contexts in Brazil
items.author: Elizabeth S. Spelke
items.content: In a preregistered, doubleblind randomized pilot study in Brazil, a game-based social-cognitive intervention improved preschool children’s emotion labeling, recognition, and emotion situation knowledge, supporting peer games for early social-emotional development.

items.title: Communicating social perspective taking creates common ground and improves relational perceptions
items.author: Hunter Gehlbach
items.content: This preregistered RCT (N = 558 U.S. adults) tested perspective-taking on a divisive environmental education topic. Affirming either arguments or intentions of the opposing side built common ground and improved relations; the former twice as effective.
